question: ช่วยหาหุ้นที่ PEG ต่ำกว่า 1 ในตลาดหุ้นสหรัฐ — ถูกเมื่อเทียบกับการเติบโต ไม่ใช่แค่ P/E ต่ำเฉยๆ (Find US stocks with PEG below 1 — cheap relative to growth, not just low P/E.)

tools_called.note: no direct PEG concept; resolved to pe + eps_diluted_growth (PEG = P/E / EPS growth%)
RELATION form: pe <= 1 x eps_diluted_growth(%). growth is in percent (e.g. 204.24) so multiple=1 == PEG<=1. All 60 rows have ratio<1.

_conventions._note: For the fields below, read the `definition` and/or `sign` before interpreting the value — a negative can MEAN something (an outflow, a benefit) and an ambiguous name needs its definition. Every other field is a plain magnitude.

eps_diluted.definition: PER SHARE, in the company's REPORTING currency (NOT USD-normalized like the _usd fields) — don't mix it with the USD amounts.

results.name: The Bank of New York Mellon Corporation

_pagination.note: Over-fetched ~4× your intended show (15) as a look-ahead buffer so 'a few more' is served from these 60 rows — do NOT re-screen for a few more. `count` is a FLOOR — the buffer filled, so MORE stocks match than shown; there is no exact market-wide total (say 'at least N', or re-screen with a larger intent / tighter filter to narrow).

answer_to_user: Modeled PEG = P/E divided by EPS growth-rate (no ready-made PEG field exists, so I used the screener's relation form: P/E lower_than EPS-growth%, which is exactly PEG < 1). Screened US common stocks. Every returned row satisfies PEG < 1 (60 matches, market-cap-ranked, buffer capped). The largest cheap-relative-to-growth names: NVDA.US PEG=0.23 (P/E 46.7 vs EPS growth 204%); GOOG.US PEG=0.93 (P/E 31.1 vs EPS growth 33%); META.US PEG=0.72 (P/E 28.7 vs EPS growth 40%); JPM.US PEG=0.87 (P/E 15.9 vs EPS growth 18%); GE.US PEG=0.10 (P/E 42.7 vs EPS growth 446%); MS.US PEG=1.00 (P/E 18.4 vs EPS growth 18%); GS.US PEG=0.94 (P/E 18.4 vs EPS growth 20%); DELL.US PEG=0.44 (P/E 16.9 vs EPS growth 39%); WFC.US PEG=0.60 (P/E 15.4 vs EPS growth 26%); KLAC.US PEG=0.27 (P/E 4.0 vs EPS growth 15%). So mega-caps like NVDA (PEG 0.23), GOOG (0.93), META (0.72), JPM (0.87), plus DELL (0.44), Wells Fargo (0.60), T-Mobile (0.28) and Disney (0.28) all screen cheap versus their growth. Caveat: growth here is trailing diluted-EPS growth (NVDA 204%, GE 446%), so a very high recent growth spurt can flatter PEG.
